topicName: API Design, Versioning, and Action Cable (WebSockets)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"API Design, Versioning, and Action Cable in Ruby on Rails"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Building modern web applications often requires combining a robust RESTful API with real-time bidirectional communication. Ruby on Rails provides built-in tools to accomplish both cleanly through namespace versioning and Action Cable for WebSockets."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Designing a Versioned API"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"API versioning ensures that changes to your data structures or endpoints do not break existing clients (such as mobile apps or older frontend builds). In Rails, namespace routing is the standard way to segregate different versions."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"Rails.application.routes.draw do
  namespace :api do
    namespace :v1 do
      resources :posts, only: [:index, :show, :create]
    end
    namespace :v2 do
      resources :posts, only: [:index, :show, :create, :update]
    end
  end
end"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Organizing Controller Namespaces"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"To match the routing configuration, controllers should be organized into corresponding directory structures under app/controllers/api/v1 and app/controllers/api/v2."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"module Api
  module V1
    class PostsController < ApplicationController
      def index
        @posts = Post.all
        render json: @posts
      end
    end
  end
end"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Introduction to Action Cable"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Action Cable seamlessly integrates WebSockets with the rest of your Rails application. It allows for real-time features like chat rooms, live notifications, and collaborative editing to be written in Ruby with the help of JavaScript on the client side."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Channels: Handle incoming and outgoing WebSocket data much like controllers handle HTTP requests."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Connections: Establish the base user context and handle authentication for the WebSocket."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Subscriptions: Manage client-side channel connections and event handlers."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Generating and Implementing a Channel"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use the Rails generator to create a new chat channel for broadcasting live messages."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"rails generate channel Chat"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Update the generated server-side channel file app/channels/chat_channel.rb to handle subscriptions and received messages."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"class ChatChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    stream_from "chat_channel"
  end

  def unsubscribed
    # Cleanup needed when channel is unsubscribed
  end

  def speak(data)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast("chat_channel", { message: data['message'] })
  end
end"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Broadcasting from Controllers or Models"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can trigger WebSocket broadcasts outside of the channel using ActionCable.server.broadcast. This is often done inside API controllers after a resource is created."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"class Api::V1::PostsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @post = Post.new(post_params)
    if @post.save
      ActionCable.server.broadcast("chat_channel", { title: @post.title })
      render json: @post, status: :created
    else
      render json: @post.errors, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end
end"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining clean API versioning namespaces with Action Cable WebSockets, your Ruby on Rails application can maintain backward-compatible REST endpoints while offering high-performance, real-time client interactions."}]
